text:
alex: heads-up — hitting sustained enqueueing on reserved pool `eu-west-2a-prod-reserved`. Admission controller started issuing deferred admits (~429 Retry-After) ~5m ago. Not seeing mass evictions yet but queue growth is steady. anyone triaging? :eyes:

maya: on it. backlog went 2.3k -> 3.8k in the last 6m, median latency spiking to 850ms. autoscale policy v3 is active, but scale events show nodes stuck in Pending. digging into node provisioning logs now.

ops-bot: [ALERT] reserved-pool-saturation: eu-west-2a-prod-reserved breach (threshold: 65% queued) — 2026-03-18T14:06:29Z.

jin: quick context — yesterday we applied the cost-savings change that reduces max GPUs per-reservation by 20% for non-enterprise pools. That could explain why headroom is lower. cc @maya @alex

sebastian: I'm seeing image pull timeouts on new hosts in eu-west region. registry egress is being rate-limited by the provider — lots of `ErrImagePull` / `context deadline exceeded` in kubelet logs. New instances are bootstrapping way slower, so autoscaler can't actually add capacity.

maya: confirmed. autoscaler reported 6 nodes Pending for >3m with `ImagePullBackOff` and `Back-off pulling image`. If nodes never join, admission controller keeps deferring.

alex: can we short-term: 1) override admission policy for tier-enterprise tenants only, 2) temporarily bump reserved-pool max cap until images finish pulling, 3) kick the node images to a local cache?

jin: i'm pushing a rollback of the cap change to restore previous max — doing a canary for this pool now. will target rollback in 2 mins.

sebastian: while rollback happens, i'll trigger cached-image deploy to eu-west local mirror, and retry bootstraps. command I'm running:```bash
kubectl -n infra exec -it image-mirror -- ./mirror-sync --region eu-west-2 --images "redwood/runner:prod-v23"```

maya: doing manual admission override: `kubectl annotate reservation eu-west-2a-prod-reserved redwood/override=admit-enterprise-only` — this should let enterprise tenants through and reduce customer impact. monitoring metrics: enterprise success rate 96% now.

ops-bot: [INFO] admission-override applied by maya at 2026-03-18T14:09:12Z

alex: nice work. jin — status on rollback?

jin: rollback applied to 1/1 canary, patching the rest now. estimated full roll back in ~4m.

sebastian: registry mirror seeding finished for the critical images, restarting the pending nodes' kubelet pods to kick the pulls. logs show image pulls progressing.

maya: backlog flattening: 3.8k -> 2.1k in 7m after override + node join. latency coming down to ~320ms.

alex: temporary mitigation looks stable. actions for postmortem: - investigate provider egress throttling (support ticket opened) - formalize a cached-image path for region bootstraps - revert admission override after pool healthy - re-evaluate cost-savings cap for reserved pools (jin)

jin: noted. will put an immediate hold on any more pool-cap reductions until we have a controlled rollout plan and regional bootstrapping tests.

sebastian: opened provider support case 789241 — they acknowledged transient egress limits correlated with maintenance window. will paste updates here.

maya: wrapping up triage, will keep monitoring for 30m then close incident if stable. thanks all :thumbsup:

ops-bot: [RESOLVED] reserved-pool-saturation eu-west-2a-prod-reserved — mitigation applied (admission override + pool cap rollback + image mirror). Incident moved to triage.
